Beats Sebastian in a Steel Cage Double Retirement Match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), reversing a back body drop into a bridging pin to end both men's own VWF careers; shakes Sebastian's hand afterward and helps fight off a post-match attack from a returning Hot Property (Stevie Knight and Austin Lee) with the Gangsta Smash.

tenures.note: Wrestles Kenny Kidd to a no-contest on Firestorm (3 May 2004) after Thunder Valenkov's own interference, then is named alongside Rob Beauty's own brother Ric in a Gauntlet 24 Hour Championship tag match. Teams with Thunder Valenkov in a 24 Hour Championship tag match against the Beauty Brothers, then enters the Gauntlet battle royal and pins Valenkov to win the VWF 24 Hour Championship himself. Attacks the Lynch Mob with his cane, Lucy, for a DQ win on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminates himself from the Dog Day One singles battle royal after assaulting a ringside official over his own 24 Hour Championship belt. Loses the Dog Day Two singles bracket's first round to LOCO, then is eliminated from the tournament, losing the VWF 24 Hour Championship match to Flash by count-out after walking off with the belt; the title does not change hands. Wrestles Daniel Sinz to a no-decision in a further 24 Hour Championship defense on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), both men walking away from the ring before a finish. Accidentally Psycho Flow DDTs tag partner Billy Bones on the outside of the ring during a six-man tag loss on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) while distracted by his own 24 Hour Championship belt. Refuses to surrender the VWF 24 Hour Championship belt when Kingston Cash declares the title no longer recognized on Wrestle Style V.1, striking Cash down; loses to a returning Classy Joey Boy by disqualification in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3 after attacking the referee rather than give up the same belt. Eliminated early from his own VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), fleeing to the back with the belt; Adam Jennings wins the battle royal and is announced champion, but Kingston Cash refuses to recognize the change unless Jennings takes the belt by force. Fails to appear for a signed follow-up against Jennings on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), ruled a no contest. Fails to appear again against Fast Eddie Cutlass on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), another no contest, then runs in with Lucy to chair Jennings after Jennings beats Kingston Cash's bodyguard G-Gangsta later the same show; Cash books Blair against Jennings in an I Quit match for the title at Vegas Violence. Loses the VWF 24 Hour Championship to Adam Jennings in an I Quit match at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), knocking out the referee and refusing to release his own grip on the belt even as Jennings works him over; finally forced to say the words after a powerslam over the top rope with both men still holding the title, then speared and sedated by ringside medics.

name: Lark Fenriz

tenures.note: Confesses on the microphone during Firestorm (26 Feb 2004) to being Classy Joey Boy's own attacker at Ghost Town Blues; interferes in the Cutlass/Equalizer match but does not wrestle one himself that night. Interrupts the Kagedo/Sidious The Clown match and wins the Team Tournament Final alongside Fast Eddie Cutlass and The Equalizer on Firestorm (3 May 2004), securing a Gauntlet entry; commentary refers to him throughout as the reigning VWF Heavyweight Champion, apparently at odds with the vacancy declared the previous Firestorm. Retains the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship in a Japanese Death Match against Sidious The Clown, then wins the Gauntlet battle royal outright over Kagedo; commentary and the ring announcer continue billing him as the reigning champion throughout, an inconsistency the reigns of record do not corroborate. Retains a claimed VWF Heavyweight Championship over Kagedo with LOCO's interference on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then wins the Dog Day One singles battle royal and the Dog Days Singles Elimination match, knocking out Daniel Sinz with brass knuckles to pin The Maquilladora. Scratched from his own three-way match by majority owner Kingston Cash on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004), sent backstage before the bell; returns to competition, without the title on the line, in the eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), targeted early and often by Morris Bass, Jason Storm and Sidious The Clown. Retains the VWF Heavyweight Championship over Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004), then wins the night's own Fourway Final on a disputed double-cover ruling by majority owner Kingston Cash to claim the Dog Day Four tournament; eliminated from the singles Pentagon of Pain on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004), spun into barbed wire by a kick meant for Jason Storm. The Heavyweight Championship main event on Wrestle Style V.1 ends without a finish when a returning Classy Joey Boy interferes; retains the title with the Sammael over a returning Billy Bones on Wrestle Style V.3, the opening defense of a new random-draw tournament. Wrestles The Predator Kevin Simmons to a time-limit draw in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004); both men advance. Retains in a fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) over Classy Joey Boy, Sebastian and The Assassin Marcus O'Malley, pinning Sebastian with the Sammael. Signs the contract for a Vegas Violence title defense against The Equalizer on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004); a video appearance by Jason Storm inserts him into the match as a third man, and the champion declares he no longer cares about the title, only about denying The Equalizer. Loses the VWF Heavyweight Championship to The Equalizer in a three-way also involving Jason Storm at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), pinned after a chair shot from guest referee Flash; Orion's own interference and a mid-match referee dispute between guest referees Classy Joey Boy and Flash both factor into the finish. Drives a forklift into the ring and canoe-paddles a trapped Flash bloody with barbed wire after Trinity's own six-man tag against Jason Storm, Fast Eddie Cutlass and Flash on March To Hell (21 October 2004), despite having no match of his own. Banned from the building at the top of March To Hell II (28 October 2004) after that attack, but slips in at the close of the night to pull The Equalizer from a brawl with Jason Storm and hit the Sammael on him. Enters the twelve-man Phear Phantastic battle royal (8 November 2004) uninvited despite the standing ban, press-slamming Iyasu Saku out for the final elimination to qualify for the Rage in the Cage, then loses the final fall of that cage match and his own VWF Heavyweight Championship challenge to The Equalizer, driven through two tables with a Face Plant after Pagan's own Final Judgement. Named on air ahead of a scheduled six-man tag against Trinity that never happens after Pagan's own video threat against Fast Eddie Cutlass on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004). Vows revenge in a taped promo, then pins Fast Eddie Cutlass with the Sammael to win a triple threat also involving Classy Joey Boy on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), the Trinity attack that follows scattered only by an unidentified woman's own three wolves. Wrestles Trinity to a no contest alongside Fast Eddie Cutlass on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005) after their own mystery third partner never arrives, nearly pinning The Equalizer before the interference began. Loses the VWF Hardcore and Submission Championship three-way to Sidious The Clown on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) after the referee mistakes his own tap on a nearby counter for champion Gods Tears's. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) and is eliminated by Classy Joey Boy's own Kiss of Death. Challenges Gods Tears and Sidious The Clown for the VWF Hardcore and Submission Championships in a Scaffold Match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), hitting the ground first after Sidious kicks both other men off the scaffold together. Loses to the debuting Mad Bomber at March To Madness (2 March 2005), powerbombed after a small explosion near the entranceway knocks him down. Ambushed in the Orleans parking lot before St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) by the same two masked men who interfered in the Equalizer and Gods Tears's own tag match the week before, powerbombed onto a Hummer's hood and hospitalized with a pierced kidney; withdrawn from the scheduled Five Way elimination match.

A debuting VXW wrestler sharing this exact ring name is independently held as sebastian-vxw, first appearing 24 December 2005, roughly two years after this record's own last documented vwf-vegas-2003 appearance and eight months after that promotion's own on-air sale and rename to VXW. tenures.note: Unmasked as the Original Masked Man after losing to Sonicman on Firestorm (27 May 2004), becomes Sonicman's manager, then wrestles a mystery-opponent match against The Equalizer, losing by disqualification; teams with Sonicman in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal, eliminating both by his own mistake. Teams with Sonicman, losing the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round to Blaze and The Real Deal, then losing again to Marcus O'Malley in a handicap match. On Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) an unidentified second Orion attacks him in his own dressing room, shown on the arena's own video screens; later interferes in The Maquilladora's own match against Sonicman, locking a submission hold on The Maquilladora before Sonicman superkicks him. Loses the VWF Submission Championship when tag partner Sonicman turns on him in a triple threat also involving The Maquilladora on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) after a chair-shot run-in by The Equalizer, then is eliminated from the Wild Card Tag Team Battle Royal alongside Sonicman on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004) by a second wrestler dressed as Orion, and attacks Kevin Blair backstage over the 24 Hour Championship, taking two Psycho Flow DDTs for it. Beat Sonicman on Wrestle Style V.1, challenged The Maquilladora unsuccessfully for the VWF Submission Championship on Wrestle Style V.2 after being blindsided by a foreign object, then beat Evil Capsman in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Beats Mark McQueen by rollup in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004). Pinned by champion Lark Fenriz with the Sammael in a Heavyweight title fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), after tricking Classy Joey Boy into a sledgehammer disqualification. Loses the six-man decider on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) when Kevin Simmons pins Robbie Caldwell, then joins Iyasu Saku, Robbie Caldwell and a returning G-Gangsta in a four-on-one beatdown of Classy Joey Boy, finishing with his own Legend Killer Piledriver. Loses with tag partner G-Gangsta by count-out to Classy Joey Boy and a returning Randall Crane at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), fleeing the ring rather than face Crane; chair-shotted unconscious backstage afterward by a vengeful Adam Jennings. Refuses to wrestle Randall Crane on March To Hell (21 October 2004), stepping aside while Robbie Caldwell tazes and beats Crane instead, ruled a disqualification loss; also fights Capsman and Evil Capsman to a no contest earlier the same show, teamed with G-Gangsta. Interferes for Gangsta against Fast Eddie Cutlass and chairs Randall Crane after Crane's own disqualification win over Robbie Caldwell on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), then offers Classy Joey Boy the Riders of the Apocalypse's own open spot, taking two Kiss of Deaths and a powerbomb for the trouble. Eliminates himself from the twelve-man Phear Phantastic battle royal (8 November 2004), diving over the top rope to keep attacking an already-eliminated Randall Crane. Beats down stablemate Iyasu Saku in an apparent staged play to draw out Paddy O'Shea on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), then wins the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse elimination match, pinning The Maquilladora after Robbie Caldwell tazes her from outside. Eliminates Evil Capsman, Capsman and, betraying tag partner Sonicman with a second Legend Killer, Sonicman himself in the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), before mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov eliminates him last. Loses a six-man tag alongside Robbie Caldwell to Mark McQueen, Thunder Valenkov and Adam Jennings on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005) after tag partner G-Gangsta fails to appear, then calls Gangsta out on the house mic and is beaten down and told of Gangsta's own resignation from the Riders of the Apocalypse. Teams with Robbie Caldwell to beat CAPSMEN! on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), earning the pair the right to book their own Ghost Town Blues matches. Hits back-to-back Legend Killers on Classy Joey Boy and The Maquilladora in the Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) fatal four-way before G-Gangsta's own Gangsta Smash finishes him for the loss; the two men are booked to retire against each other at Ghost Town Blues. Loses to G-Gangsta in a Steel Cage Double Retirement Match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), pinned when Gangsta reverses a back body drop into a bridge, ending both men's own VWF careers; raises Gangsta's hand afterward and helps fight off a post-match attack from a returning Hot Property (Stevie Knight and Austin Lee) with the Legend Killer.

The promotion's first 24 Hour Champion, in August 2001, and champion again that month; wrestled masked against Kerry Powell before his unmasking; BWF President from Halloween 2001. Lost to Jack Spade by disqualification, teamed with Tai Angela Classy Joey Boy Maquilladora, lost Maquilladora at Ghost Town Blues. Appears across VWF documents, February June 2002.

name: Ric Beauty
caption: Lost Re-RAW's second-ever match teaming with Arron Iron, then avenged it three weeks later as one half of the newly self-named team Sexual Assault.

tenures.note: Runs in with a chair against Christian Demonstone before the bell on Firestorm (26 Feb 2004) and is presented afterward by Blackbird as the newest member of the New Age Army. Arrives at ringside as VWF 24 Hour Champion during the Kidd/Blair match on Firestorm (3 May 2004) and is blindsided by Thunder Valenkov, then needles his brother Rob into a Beauty Brothers tag match for the title at the Gauntlet. Wrestles for the VWF 24 Hour Championship on the Gauntlet, teaming with his own brother Rob against Kevin Blair and Thunder Valenkov; pinned by Valenkov to lose the title. Joins Dan The Man Aller on color commentary for New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), introduced by JD Southerns as a holdover from the 12 Days Tournament. Visits Classy Joey Boy backstage at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), blaming him for letting the company slip into government hands and promising the Beauty Brothers will win the coming auction. Joins his brothers Rob and Rod in attacking Classy Joey Boy in the Orleans parking lot before End Of March (30 March 2005). Joins his brothers Rob and Rod in a three-on-one handicap match against Classy Joey Boy on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), disqualified alongside them when Rod Beauty picks up the barred sledgehammer.

Billed "The Bi-Polar Brawler" and "The 24 Hour Man," the same aka names as his already-held vwf-vegas-2003 and re-raw tenures; cuts a promo on Winter War II wearing a rival wrestler's own tournament medals, then wrestles and wins on Winter War III. Returns on Ghost Town Blues to beat Lean Darlene Orion by submission in a repeat Scott Starring Medal Challenge, then addresses the crowd as part owner of the VXW ahead of the unsanctioned Simmons/Kagedo main event. Refuses Chris Wheeling's demand for an immediate Twenty-Four Hour title rematch on Xtreme Machine I, citing Roman Anderson's own open title-shot contract, then argues in the ring with his brother Rod over the loss of Rod's own 49 percent VXW stake. Wins a comedic non-tournament exhibition bout over a hot dog vendor pulled from the stands on The Hype II, retaining Scott Starring's own Twelve Days Tournament medals. Does not appear on The Hype I. Cuts a Twelve Days Medal Challenge promo on The Hype IV and is attacked by a visiting Shootfire wrestler, Jeff Keenan, before retreating to the back without wrestling; does not appear on The Hype III or The Gauntlet, where his brother Rod reports he was unable to attend.

Rob Beauty's brother and Kerry Powell's rival from their shared past, who founded the BWF faction inside the VWF in 2001, lost a Loser Leaves Nevada match at Vegas Violence and left the VWF by letter in November 2001.
Returned to the VWF, sold his BWF stake back to his brother Rob Beauty, and joined Dan The Man Aller on commentary for Ghost Town Blues.

Beats Roadkill Rick at End Of March (30 March 2005) with a schoolboy and a handful of tights after valet Blackbird distracts him. Rolls up and eliminates Fast Eddie Cutlass in the eight-man elimination match on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), then is pinned in the match's final fall by Adam Jennings's small package after blocking a Hyper Driver.

Appears across VWF documents, February June 2002.

caption: A heavyweight billed as "The Dark Monster," beaten by Kagedo in the opener of Xtreme Prejudice VI.

name: Lance Voltar

tenures.note: Lost a handicap match alongside Blake Hamilton to The Outlaw Morris Bass at Sin City Fights October 16, both men finished off with a Widowmaker apiece, one delivered on the ring steps. Loses to Paddy O'Shea on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), caught with a top-rope Fist Drop after knocking O'Shea dizzy with an early flurry. Billed The Big V, submits to Kenny Kidd's Elko Lasso on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) after Billy Bones interferes from ringside, then loses a backstage challenge match to Capsman for Ghost Town Blues. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005), eliminates Evil Capsman, and is eliminated alongside CAPSMAN by Sidious The Clown and Kagedo before climbing back onto the apron to legdrop and pin CAPSMAN himself. Loses a Loser Is Winners Valet Match to CAPSMAN at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005) after his own missed top-rope Twisting Corkscrew Legdrop bumps the referee and CAPSMAN schoolboys him once the referee revives, becoming CAPSMAN's own ringside valet. Rolls dice on the Orleans craps table at March To Madness (2 March 2005), chanting for a shot at Frank O'Shea. Faces Paddy O'Shea at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) in a match that ends without a decision when a returning Capsman runs in and chases off both O'Sheas, becoming Capsman's own ringside valet after the prior show's own Loser Is Winners Valet Match. Teams with Capsman against The O'Sheas at End Of March (30 March 2005), pinned after a top-rope fist drop from Paddy. Wins his first match, teaming with Capsman against The O'Sheas on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), pinning Paddy O'Shea after kicking him off a schoolboy attempt. Enters the closing Gauntlet battle royal, tossing out debuting Stan Klenski before being eliminated himself minutes later.

Half of Dudes of Destruction on Xtreme Prejudice VI. Wrestles on the losing side of the six-man tag scramble on Sin City Fights August 31; distracts the referee to help fellow Dude of Destruction Blake Hamilton beat The Outlaw Morris Bass on Sin City Fights September 11, then loses a Russian Chain Match to Thunder Valenkov; wins Ring Two of the TV Title Open Match on Sin City Fights September 19, earning a VXW Spin The Wheel Television Championship shot against Justin Harper at Vegas Violence. Lost to Justin Harper's own Television Championship defense at Vegas Violence 2006, then joined a returning Blake Hamilton in attacking The Outlaw Morris Bass after the Tag Team Title scramble, striking him with his own surfboard.

caption: Turned on his own tag partners to form Dudes of Destruction, winning by disqualification on Xtreme Prejudice VI after a surfboard-breaking dropkick set him off.

name: Kenny Kidd

tenures.note: Wrestles Kevin Blair to a no-contest on Firestorm (3 May 2004) after Thunder Valenkov's own interference. Teams with Billy Bones to win the VWF Tag Team Championship in the Gauntlet's own Four Corners match, then enters the battle royal, eliminating Evil Capsman before being eliminated himself. Loses the VWF Tag Team Championship to Hot Property in a Flashback ambush on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then wins the Dog Day One tag team battle royal with Billy Bones. Teams with Billy Bones as the Rodeo Boys, losing the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round to Marcus O'Malley wrestling alone, then beaten down by Hot Property and Flash in a special Flashback and competing in the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), falling from the ladder alongside Stevie Knight. Loses a six-man tag on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) after accidentally being DDT'd by his own partner Kevin Blair, then is hurt and removed by medics during the Dog Days Four Tag Team Scramble after a disqualification win, before being eliminated from the Wild Card Tag Team Battle Royal with tag partner Billy Bones on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004). Lost to Mr. Electricity Robbie Caldwell on both Wrestle Style V.2 and the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3, both times distracted by his missing tag partner Billy Bones; present ringside for Bones's own rehab reveal and title match loss to Lark Fenriz on Wrestle Style V.3, after which Kingston Cash releases both Rodeo Boys from their contracts. Brands Marcus O'Malley on the lower back with a branding iron for a disqualification loss to the VWF Tag Team Champions on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Loses the title rematch on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), yanking Outlaw Morris Bass off the ring apron during the match. Retrieves the branding iron again to clang The Salvation and set up Billy Bones's own winning pin in a weapons-advantage Number One Contenders match at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004). Helps eliminate Capsman first in the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse elimination match on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004) with the Double Eight Second Ride, before being small-packaged by The Maquilladora. Eliminated by Thunder Valenkov in the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004). Submits The Reckoning with the Ankle Lock on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), tag partner Billy Bones working the same leg over with a chair from ringside throughout. Billed The New Revolution Kenny Kidd, submits Lance Voltar with the Elko Lasso on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) after Billy Bones interferes from ringside. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005), working Classy Joey Boy's own ankle before Classy Joey Boy flips him over the top rope. Makes Mark McQueen tap to the Elko Lasso in the Rings Of Glory match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), but Thunder Valenkov, already through his own half of the match, finishes him alone with the Thunder Bomb as the Rodeo Boys fall short of the VWF Tag Team Championship. Beats Fast Eddie Cutlass at March To Madness (2 March 2005) with a small package, then distracts the referee for Riders of the Apocalypse stablemate Mr Electricity Robbie Caldwell's own win over Thunder Valenkov. Loses to Caldwell at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) after Caldwell talks him into a receiving a fall first, then wins a real fight before Caldwell rolls him up. Teams with Billy Bones as the Rodeo Boys against Sidious The Clown and Kagedo at End Of March (30 March 2005), forcing Sidious to tap to the Elko Lasso; demands and is granted a spot in The Gauntlet's own eight-man elimination match afterward. Competes on the losing side of the eight-man elimination match on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), counted out brawling with Tai Angela's own manager Blackbird at ringside. Enters the closing Gauntlet battle royal as its second entrant, the first man eliminated, tossed out by champion The Equalizer after Revolution Randall Crane's surprise return breaks Kidd's own Elko Lasso submission hold.

Announced his own retirement from VXW at Xtreme Machine I (8 March 2006, an earlier pass). Returned with Billy Bones to make the save for a beaten Joey Young and Tom Rogers against POT on New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, then beat POT (Lark Fenriz and Foodstamp) by pinfall as the Rodeo Boys on Sin City Fights February 7, billing it their own 'last ride' and challenging the O'Malleys, Team Brittania and Hot Property to a tag team tournament.

caption: Billed as "The New Perfect Storm," pinned by the original Jason Storm on Xtreme Prejudice VI after a run-in from two of the promotion's own veterans.

name: Iyasu Saku

tenures.note: Joins Thunder Valenkov and Blackbird in a backstage ambush of Kevin Simmons on Firestorm (3 May 2004), then is challenged to a Hair vs. Title Submission Championship match at the Gauntlet. Already billed as VWF Submission Champion, retains against Kevin Simmons in a Hair vs. Hair match, then enters the Gauntlet battle royal and loses the title by submission to The Maquilladora. Submitted to Kevin Simmons's Durham Deathlock for the New Age Army in the ten-man tag loss to the Society of Doom on Wrestle Style V.1. Returns from a shock absence during Wrestle Style V.4's own Caldwell-Bass tournament match (10 September 2004). Pins Sonicman with the Roaring Elbow to open Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), applying the Good and Evil Crossface after the bell until a six-man brawl is ruled a no contest; his own wife Lindsay Simmons later distracts husband Kevin Simmons at ringside. Loses the six-man decider on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) when Kevin Simmons pins Robbie Caldwell, Morris Bass grabbing his own ankle to stop the save. Interferes in the Capsman-Evil Capsman-Gangsta-Sebastian match on March To Hell (21 October 2004), then loses the VWF 24 Hour Championship match to Adam Jennings by pinfall (Hyper Driver) the same show, the Riders of the Apocalypse unable to make the save. Loses to Classy Joey Boy on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), caught with the Kiss of Death out of midair; the Riders attack him afterward rather than CJB. Last man eliminated from the twelve-man Phear Phantastic battle royal (8 November 2004), pressed over Lark Fenriz's own head and out. Beaten down by stablemates Sebastian, G-Gangsta and Robbie Caldwell in an apparent staged play to draw out Paddy O'Shea on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004). Eliminated from the tag team title battle royal alongside The Maquilladora by a charging Roadkill Rick on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), after taking shots at Rick earlier in the match.

caption: A long-tenured VXW wrestler, returning from time away to open Xtreme Prejudice VII with a pinfall win over Sonicman.

name: Evil Capsman

tenures.note: Wrestled as The Rhombus's own "CAPSMAN," tagging with the real Capsman's regular partner Sonicman, before turning on Sonicman mid-match and unmasking as the impostor. Infiltrates The Rhombus's own corner disguised as Capsman again at Ghost Town Blues, costing Sonicman the match, then teams legitimately with the real Capsman as "Capsmen" on Firestorm (26 Feb 2004). Teams legitimately with the real Capsman to beat Blaze and The Real Deal on Firestorm (3 May 2004), scoring the pin with the Evil Capitol Punishment. Teams with Capsman to open the Gauntlet, pinning Blaze, then enters the battle royal and is eliminated by Kenny Kidd. Loses to The Mistress on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then his own team is eliminated by The Salvation in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal. Teams with Capsman as CAPSMEN! in the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round, losing to The Mighty Men, then competes in the sixteen-man Dog Days 3 tag scramble and is eliminated from the tournament in the Tag Team Elimination Ladder Match on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Loses to the Unholy Alliance on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) after offering The Mistress a rose, then is eliminated from the Wild Card Tag Team Battle Royal with tag partner Capsman on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004). Tapped out to Orion's Drunken Rage on Wrestle Style V.1 alongside tag partner Capsman, then lost to Sebastian in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Helps eliminate champion Kevin Blair early from the VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004). Loses the VWF Tag Team Championship match to Blaze and Real Deal by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after The Mighty Men run in. Submits to Paddy O'Shea's own Chicken Wing, losing a six-man tag with Capsman and Sonicman (billed together as The Rhombus) to The Mighty Men and a returning O'Shea at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004). Rolls dice at March To Madness (2 March 2005), one of five men Kingston Cash books into a St Patricks Day elimination match. Attacked backstage by Paddy and Frank O'Shea before St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) and hospitalized, withdrawn from the elimination match.

caption: Capsman's own former partner, eliminated from the Rhombus Rumble alongside him by a double dropkick from The Maquilladora.

tenures.note: Attacked by an unseen figure near a creek before Ghost Town Blues's own Pentagon match and hospitalized, unable to defend the VWF Heavyweight Championship; ruled out at least six weeks on Firestorm (26 Feb 2004), where the title is declared vacant pending a Gauntlet tournament, though he does not appear on that broadcast. Returns on Wrestle Style V.1, interfering with a sledgehammer in the Heavyweight Championship main event; cuts a lengthy promo on Wrestle Style V.2 disputing Lark Fenriz's claim to the title and asserting he was never properly stripped of it; wins over Kevin Blair by disqualification in the opening round of the new VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Wins by count-out over a no-show Jason Storm in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004) after The Equalizer attacks him from the crowd with the timekeeper's bell. Disqualified in a Heavyweight title fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) after Sebastian tricks him into a sledgehammer shot; hits Sebastian with the Kiss of Death and a Studd Splash regardless before officials pull the two apart. Teams with a returning Randall Crane against Sebastian and G-Gangsta in a handicap match turned even at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), won by count-out when the Legends flee the ring; later shares guest-referee duties, and blows, with Flash during the VWF Heavyweight Championship main event. Present for Kingston Cash's own backstage suspension of Flash on March To Hell (21 October 2004), then wrestles Lark Fenriz to a time-limit draw. Seconds The Maquilladora's own Submission Championship match and beats Iyasu Saku (Kiss of Death out of midair) to earn a Rage in the Cage spot on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), then feigns accepting Sebastian's own offer to join the Riders of the Apocalypse before powerbombing him and dropping Kiss of Deaths on G-Gangsta and Robbie Caldwell. Eliminated from the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), pinned by Fast Eddie Cutlass after Lark Fenriz's own Sammael. Named on air ahead of a scheduled six-man tag against Trinity that never happens on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004). Loses a triple threat also involving Lark Fenriz and Fast Eddie Cutlass on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), pinned by neither man in the final fall. Fights The Maquilladora to a double count-out draw on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005). Challenges The Equalizer for the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship alongside The Maquilladora on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), using his own 25% ownership stake to book himself into the match over majority owner Kingston Cash's objection. Loses to Sebastian and G-Gangsta in the Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) fatal four-way, then eliminates Billy Bones, Lark Fenriz, Sidious The Clown and Kenny Kidd in the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet before Adam Jennings eliminates him. Loses the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship match to champion The Equalizer and The Maquilladora in a Wheel Of Chaos match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005) after a doctor, revealed afterward as Kingston Cash's own brother Terrance Cash, injects him mid-match. Teams with The Maquilladora against The Equalizer and Gods Tears at March To Madness (2 March 2005), the match declared a no contest after two masked men interfere on both sides; the IRS seizes his own 25% ownership stake in the VWF the same night, alongside Kingston Cash's majority share. Pulled from the scheduled Five Way elimination match at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) with a flare-up of a long-standing knee and ankle injury. Attacked in the parking lot by all three Beauty Brothers before End Of March (30 March 2005); John Tyler books a three-on-one match against them for The Gauntlet, allowing Classy Joey Boy a sledgehammer. Beats all three Beauty Brothers by disqualification in a three-on-one handicap match on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005) after Rod Beauty picks up the sledgehammer barred from the Beautys' own use, then enters the closing Gauntlet battle royal as its fourth entrant, thrown out by Justin Davidson.

BWF Champion by 20 December 2001. Saw the Championship renamed Blackjack on air and retained it through month, including a No Holds Barred defense against Tai Angela at Ghost Town Blues. Appears across VWF documents, February to June 2002.

name: The Maquilladora
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2003: #140, with no federation named beside the entry. caption: Came in at #140 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 2003.

tenures.note: Serves as guest referee, alongside Demonic, in the Capsmen/Blaze and Real Deal match on Firestorm (3 May 2004), without wrestling herself. Wins a Loser Retires, I Quit match over Demonic, then enters the Gauntlet battle royal and makes Iyasu Saku submit to the Bow and Arrow, winning the VWF Submission Championship. Teams with Kevin Blair against the Lynch Mob on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminated from the Dog Day One singles battle royal by LOCO before being pinned by Lark Fenriz in the Dog Days Singles Elimination match. Retains the VWF Submission Championship by disqualification against Daniel Sinz on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004) after he strikes her with a chair. Wins a non-title match against Sonicman by disqualification on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) after he decks the referee and Sebastian interferes. Loses the VWF Submission Championship to Sonicman in a triple threat also involving Sebastian on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004). Already billed VWF Submission Champion by Wrestle Style V.2, having regained the title off-page since Dog Day Four; retained against Sebastian after Sonicman blindsided him, then lost to Marcus O'Malley in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Wrestles Fast Eddie Cutlass to a non-title time-limit draw on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004). Pins Flash with the Permanent Daylight in the seven-man mini rumble on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), then loses to Cutlass after an unidentified woman slaps him twice at ringside; Kingston Cash books the loss as a VWF Submission Championship match at Vegas Violence. Wrestles Fast Eddie Cutlass to a no contest for the VWF Submission Championship at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004) after Orion, Orion #2 and The Equalizer run in on both competitors. Helps Sonicman clear a four-on-two beatdown of Capsman and Evil Capsman on March To Hell (21 October 2004), an unidentified woman blowing him a kiss on screen afterward. Retains the VWF Submission Championship despite a count-out loss to Gods Tears on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), distracted when the same woman surfaces from the crowd to kiss him mid-match. Submits to Gods Tears's own Drunken Rage in the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), losing the title for real. Outlasts three Rhombus stablemates in the eight-man Rhombus/Riders of the Apocalypse elimination match on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), eliminating G-Gangsta, Kenny Kidd and Billy Bones before being tazed from outside by Robbie Caldwell and pinned by Sebastian. Eliminated from the tag team title battle royal on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004) alongside Iyasu Saku by a charging Roadkill Rick, the unidentified woman who has been stalking him interfering again first. Fights Classy Joey Boy to a double count-out draw on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005). Challenges The Equalizer for the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship alongside Classy Joey Boy on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), breaking up a cover on the champion before being pinned with the Face Plant. Loses to Sebastian and G-Gangsta in the Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) fatal four-way. Loses the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship match to champion The Equalizer and Classy Joey Boy in a Wheel Of Chaos match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005) after a doctor, revealed afterward as Kingston Cash's own brother Terrance Cash, injects her mid-match. Teams with Classy Joey Boy against The Equalizer and Gods Tears at March To Madness (2 March 2005), the match declared a no contest after two masked men interfere on both sides. Beats Henry Fish, billed Scott Starring, at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) with Permanent Daylight after confronting him over the real Scott Starring's own record. Loses to Mr Electricity Robbie Caldwell at End Of March (30 March 2005), Shock And Horror off the top rope moments after The Mad Bomber blinds her with a flash of light. Beats Robbie Caldwell with the Permanent Daylight on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), then enters the closing Gauntlet battle royal, eliminating Revolution Randall Crane with a diving hurricanrana that also carries The Maquilladora himself over the top rope.

A newcomer in the promotion's 12 Days tournament of December 2001, challenging for T3 Title on 20 2001. Beat The Ghost, lost to Xtreme Tony Cage, then teamed with Classy Joey Boy and beat Sebastian twice, including at Ghost Town Blues. Appears across VWF documents, February June 2002.

name: Stan Klenski

tenures.note: Debuts with a win over The Mad Bomber, a Full Nelson Face First off the top rope, then enters the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal as its eighth entrant, tossed out by CAPSMAN with a dropkick near the ropes.

Wrestled again as 'The Polish Bulldog,' losing to a returning Adam Lazarus by pinfall on Sin City Fights November 18. Beat Foodstamp by count-out on Sin City Fights November 27 after Roman Anderson and John Manning ran in to save Foodstamp's own tabled opponent, then Lark Fenriz cleared the ring.

caption: A vwf-vegas-2003 wrestler ("The Polish Bulldog") who debuted with a win over the Mad Bomber in April 2005, resurfacing on VXW's own Ghost Town Blues card as an ally of Sebastian's.

name: The Equalizer
notes: Known only from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 2004: #109, tagged VWF. Carries no tenure entry: none of the tagged federations is a held promotion, and the poll records where a wrestler was tagged, never a run this record could date.
caption: Came in at #109 in the RSPWF Top 200 for 2004, tied with three others at that placing.

tenures.note: Guests on Flash's own new interview segment, THE FLASHBACK, interrupted by Sidious The Clown, then wins the Team Tournament Final alongside Lark Fenriz and Fast Eddie Cutlass on Firestorm (3 May 2004), securing a Gauntlet entry. Loses a triple threat to Kagedo after an unidentified masked attacker's interference, then enters the Gauntlet battle royal and is eliminated by Kagedo and Marcus O'Malley together. Wins by disqualification against Sebastian on Firestorm (27 May 2004) after Sonicman's interference, then teams with Orion in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal, eliminated in a mutual elimination alongside him. Teams with Orion in the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round, losing to Marcus O'Malley wrestling alone; overpowers several rivals in the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), attempting and failing to unmask the ring's own Orion after the video screens show a second Orion elsewhere. Disqualified alongside Billy Bones in the Dog Days Four Tag Team Scramble on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) after three chair shots, then wins the Wild Card Tag Team Battle Royal and the tag Pentagon of Pain with Orion The Hunter on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004) to reach the Dog Days tag final. Won alongside Orion The Hunter on Wrestle Style V.1, attacked the referee before a signed tag match could begin on Wrestle Style V.2, then beat Real Deal in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Beats Blaze with a Face Plant onto Blaze's own steel chair in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), then attacks a no-show Jason Storm's scheduled opponent Classy Joey Boy from the crowd with the timekeeper's bell. Outlasts Robbie Caldwell, The Outlaw Morris Bass and The Predator Kevin Simmons in a fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) to earn the Vegas Violence title match, pinning Simmons with a Face Plant after Lindsay Simmons distracts her own husband. Signs the contract for that match on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004); Jason Storm crashes the signing by video and blows up his truck. Part of Trinity's six-man tag win over Jason Storm, Fast Eddie Cutlass and Flash on March To Hell (21 October 2004). Helps beat down his own ally Flash in the Flashback segment on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), then is ambushed by Jason Storm after demanding a fight of his own, beaten bloody with a chair before Lark Fenriz interferes with a Sammael. Retains the VWF Heavyweight Championship over Lark Fenriz in the final fall of the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), hitting a Face Plant through two tables after Pagan's own Final Judgement weakens the challenger. Helps Gods Tears and Pagan attack a beaten Fast Eddie Cutlass, Lark Fenriz and Classy Joey Boy after Pagan's own video threat cancels their scheduled six-man tag on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004). Runs in against Kingston Cash's own year-end Trinity suspension to join the post-match beatdown of Lark Fenriz and Fast Eddie Cutlass on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), scattered by an unidentified woman's own three wolves. Knocks Sidious The Clown from the ring and joins Gods Tears and Pagan's own no-contest brawl with Fast Eddie Cutlass and Lark Fenriz on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005). Retains the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship against The Maquilladora and Classy Joey Boy on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) after Sebastian's interference and a guest-referee stint from majority owner Kingston Cash. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) as the surprise final three-man entry alongside Pagan and Gods Tears, eliminated last by Thunder Valenkov. Retains the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship over Classy Joey Boy and The Maquilladora in a Wheel Of Chaos match at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005) after a doctor who slips into the cage stipulation to treat the bleeding champion instead injects both challengers, letting The Equalizer pin them once they collapse; the doctor is revealed afterward as Kingston Cash's own brother, Terrance Cash. Also joins Gods Tears in interfering for Pagan against Fast Eddie Cutlass earlier the same show, toppling a ringside spotlight onto Cutlass before enforcer Kagedo breaks it up. Teams with Gods Tears against Classy Joey Boy and The Maquilladora at March To Madness (2 March 2005), the match declared a no contest after two masked men interfere on both sides. His own scheduled VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship defense against Kagedo at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) is aborted before the bell when Gods Tears attacks Kagedo with a tire iron; John Tyler books a bonus tag match instead, and The Equalizer and Gods Tears are disqualified against Kagedo and Roadkill Rick when Gods Tears breaks up a near-fall with the tire iron. Retains the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), entering the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal first by his own request rather than last as tradition dictates and surviving as the sole man left in the ring after Thunder Valenkov, sent into a top rope that Hot Property forgets to pull down, goes over instead.
Sandbagged from behind by his own Trinity partner Sebastian's own directed gang attack (Miles McKinley and the Dierdorfs) on Sin City Fights November 27, pinned by Brian Dierdorf's Pulverizer.

name: "Modern Messiah" Setzer Van Strife
caption: One half of the returning heel duo the Lynch Mob, debuting on the Kickoff Card with a Short Armed Yakuza Kick and a Straight Jacket Suplex that put down both Legends of the VWF.

tenures.note: Loses the Team Tournament Final alongside LOCO on Firestorm (3 May 2004). The Lynch Mob, defending champions, are eliminated first in the Gauntlet's own Four Corners Tag Team Championship match, Stevie Knight submitting LOCO with a sharpshooter. Teams with LOCO as the Lynch Mob against Kevin Blair and The Maquilladora on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminates himself from the Dog Day One singles battle royal chasing Kevin Blair up the ramp. Loses the Dog Day Two singles bracket's first round to The Outlaw Morris Bass, then wins the eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), naming LOCO and Lord Zero for that night's singles elimination match. Wins the Dog Days Four Singles Six Man on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) with the Fallen Angels Wings, loses the Fourway Final, then is eliminated from the singles Pentagon of Pain by Jason Storm on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004) after bloodying him with barbed wire post-match.

Cut a comeback promo describing years away from the ring running a wrestling school in Chicago and heading Lynch Mob Productions, a film company; said he tracked down a copy of a Night of Champions broadcast and decided to return upon learning Alex Martinez, a wrestler he said he came up alongside, was UWF World Heavyweight Champion. Named Martinez his own target and declared himself the UWF's newest arrival. Did not wrestle.

identity.note: Name collision only: two RSPWF Top 200 poll stubs carry a similarly spelled name (2000 and 2003 editions tagged GLOW/OWE; a 2004 edition tagged WILD/BWA+), none tagged VWF; nothing ties either poll placement to this in-fiction debut.
An RSPWF Top 200 stub and a held IWE record carry a wrestler of the same name under a different nickname, "2 Smooth"; nothing in this record's own promo ties it to either beyond the bare name.

name: LOCO
caption: The other half of the returning heel duo the Lynch Mob, debuting on the Kickoff Card by hanging Sebastian over the top rope and striking him with a broken Singapore Cane.

tenures.note: Loses the Team Tournament Final on Firestorm (3 May 2004), pinned by Fast Eddie Cutlass. The Lynch Mob, defending champions, are eliminated first in the Gauntlet's own Four Corners Tag Team Championship match, submitting to Stevie Knight's sharpshooter. Teams with Setzer Van Strife as the Lynch Mob against Kevin Blair and The Maquilladora on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminates Sidious The Clown and The Maquilladora before eliminating himself from the Dog Day One singles battle royal. Wins the Dog Day Two singles bracket's first round over Kevin Blair and Lord Zero, then helps The Outlaw Morris Bass win the semifinal over Jason Storm. Competes in the eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), then is eliminated from the tournament in the Dog Days Three Singles Elimination Match against Lord Zero after an unidentified masked man interferes.

identity.note: Name collision only: this wing already holds an unrelated wrestler ring-named El Gringo Loco, active earlier the same broadcast as a reigning tag champion, and the bare ring name LOCO recurs across several unconnected wings and an RSPWF poll stub; nothing in this debut ties the Lynch Mob's own LOCO to any of them.

name: Kail
caption: One of two allies who broke Kevin Blair out of the Nevada State Mental Institution, arrested at ringside on the Kickoff Card before the count-out.

name: Sinclair
caption: The other ally who broke Kevin Blair out of the Nevada State Mental Institution, arrested at ringside on the Kickoff Card before the count-out.

name: Fallen Angel David Cross
caption: A wrestler who won a Falls Count Anywhere match by count-out on Firestorm, January 19, 2004, after his opponent Lance Voltar left the ring to confront Classy Joey Boy and never returned.

name: Ali Collymore
caption: A rookie who never gained a foothold on the VWF roster, pinned by the debuting Fallen Angel David Cross's own Ashes to Ashes in his Firestorm try-out.

tenures.note: Appears across VWF documents, February to June 2002.

name: Dane Klingel
caption: One half of a VWF enhancement pairing wrestling under The Enforcers banner, pinned in his debut when the Society of Doom's Kagedo hit a Dragon Suplex on his tag partner.

tenures.note: Appears across VWF documents, February to June 2002.

name: Rob Kidane
caption: One half of a VWF enhancement pairing wrestling under The Enforcers banner, pinned by a Kagedo Dragon Suplex in his debut.

tenures.note: Lost to the debuting Mr. Electricity Robbie Caldwell on Wrestle Style V.1. Pinned by a debuting Phoenix Adam Lazarus with the Phoenix Effect on March To Hell II (28 October 2004).
Appears across VWF documents, February to June 2002.

name: Christian Demonstone
caption: A RAW-Carolina alumnus who once took that promotion's own Heavyweight Championship from Ric Beauty, debuting in the VWF against Iyasu Saku only to be chair-shotted from behind by Beauty before the bell settled.

name: Johnny King
caption: A brawling cruiserweight newcomer, tapping out to Kevin Simmons's own Modified Durham Deathlock in his lone attested appearance.

name: The Real Deal
caption: A tag partner Blaze brought in for a guest-refereed match against the Capsmen, on the losing side when Evil Capsman pinned Blaze.

identity.note: Shares a common ring name exactly with two other wings' own wrestlers; no document connects any of them.

tenures.note: Teams with Blaze against the Society of Doom on Firestorm (27 May 2004), chairing both O'Malley and McQueen after the bell, then eliminates The Salvation and Dementia in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal before his own team is eliminated. Teams with Blaze to win the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round over Sonicman and Sebastian with a Chokeslam to Hell, then is beaten down and hospitalized by Hot Property after the bell. Wins the Dog Days Three Tag Team Elimination Ladder Match on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), recovering the ring after the ladder snaps under him and Dementia. Already billed VWF Tag Team Champion alongside Blaze by Wrestle Style V.2, having regained the titles off-page since losing them earlier that spring; retained against the Society of Doom by disqualification, then lost to The Equalizer in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Beats Mark McQueen by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) after stablemate Marcus O'Malley interferes on McQueen's behalf. Retains the VWF Tag Team Championship with Blaze by disqualification over Capsman and Evil Capsman on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after The Mighty Men break up a Capsman near-fall on him. Taps to Mark McQueen's own Devils Snare, losing the VWF Tag Team Championship with Blaze to Alcoholics Anonymous (Marcus O'Malley and Mark McQueen) at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004).
Arrived in September 2001 as the RCW's seven-foot-four member. Eliminated from four-way T3 Title match, then won VWF Tag Team Championship with Blaze. Appears across documents, February to June 2002.

name: Jack Smash
caption: Half of the enhancement pairing Jumping Jacks Flash, pinned alongside his own similarly-named partner by The Unholy Alliance.

tenures.note: Runs in on Evil Capsman on Firestorm (27 May 2004) and announces the new ring name Jack Smash, then eliminated by Billy Bones in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal before being pinned by Hot Property in the Dog Days Tag Team Elimination match.

name: Jack Blast
caption: Half of the enhancement pairing Jumping Jacks Flash, pinned by Dementia's own spinning powerbomb after a Mistress spinning heel kick.

tenures.note: Runs in on Evil Capsman on Firestorm (27 May 2004) and announces the new ring name Jack Blast, then survives the Dog Day One tag team battle royal to elimination before being pinned by Hot Property in the Dog Days Tag Team Elimination match.

name: Dementia
caption: The large, mostly silent half of The Unholy Alliance, pinning Flash Jack with a spinning powerbomb in the pairing's first confirmed appearance.

identity.note: Shares a name exactly with another wing's own wrestler; no document connects them.

tenures.note: Teams with The Mistress as the Unholy Alliance in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal, saving her before being clotheslined out. Teams with The Mistress as the Unholy Alliance again on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004), eliminated in the first round of the tag bracket by The Mighty Men, then reaches the top of the ladder together with The Real Deal in the Dog Days Three Tag Team Elimination Ladder Match on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), both crashing down when it snaps. Wins a tag match over Capsmen on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) alongside The Mistress; The Unholy Alliance is announced absent from Dog Day Five (16 July 2004) on personal leave.

name: The Mistress
caption: The talking half of The Unholy Alliance, whose video evidence of a Lynch Mob bribery scheme forced Rob Beauty into booking a four-way Tag Team Championship match at the Gauntlet.

tenures.note: Teams with Dementia as the Unholy Alliance in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal. Teams with Dementia as the Unholy Alliance again on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004), pinned by The Salvation in the tag bracket's first round, then eliminated again in the Dog Days Three Tag Team Elimination Ladder Match on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Rolls up Capsman for the win over Capsmen on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004) alongside Dementia; The Unholy Alliance is announced absent from Dog Day Five (16 July 2004) on personal leave.

name: Sidious The Clown
caption: A crude, comedic heel wrestled to a distraction-finish loss against Kagedo, teased for a Japanese Death Match against Lark Fenriz at the Gauntlet.

tenures.note: Challenges Lark Fenriz for the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship in a Japanese Death Match, going through the ring's own timed pyrotechnic explosion at the finish and losing by pinfall. Eliminated by LOCO in the Dog Day One singles battle royal. Loses to Jason Storm on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004) after champion Lark Fenriz is scratched from their billed three-way. Competes in the eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), speared off the ladder by Setzer Van Strife. Wins the Dog Days Four Singles Six Man alongside Setzer Van Strife and The Outlaw Morris Bass on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004), loses the Fourway Final, then is eliminated from the Dog Days tournament by The Outlaw in a singles elimination match the same night; brawls to a double countout with Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004). Works the New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005) main event as special guest referee, knocked from the ring by The Equalizer and later assaulted on the arena's own big screens by Gods Tears with a lead pipe, prompting new VWF guardian John Tyler's own on-air intervention. Wins the VWF Submission Championship from Gods Tears in a three-way also involving Lark Fenriz on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) after the referee mistakes Fenriz's own tap on a nearby counter for the champion's. Enters the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) and is eliminated by Classy Joey Boy's own enziguiri. Retains the VWF Submission Championship in a Scaffold Match also involving Gods Tears and Lark Fenriz at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), swinging out on an overhead rigging line to kick both other men off the scaffold together; Fenriz hits the ground first and the match is awarded to Sidious, though the broadcast states neither the VWF Hardcore nor Submission Championship changes hands. Retains the VWF Submission Championship against Tazmanian Devil Mark McQueen at March To Madness (2 March 2005), putting McQueen out with a sleeper after an unexplained arena blackout leaves both men down. Defends the title against Fast Eddie Cutlass at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), declared a no contest after Gods Tears, Roadkill Rick, Adam Jennings and The Dark Monster Tai Angela all converge on Gods Tears mid-match. Teams with Kagedo against the Rodeo Boys at End Of March (30 March 2005), tapping out to Kenny Kidd's own Elko Lasso. Loses the VWF Submission Championship to Roadkill Rick, submitting to the Texas Speedbump, in an eight-man elimination match on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005) after Gods Tears attacks him from behind before the bell; also enters the closing Gauntlet battle royal, eliminated when Classy Joey Boy flips him out of the ring off an errant handspring.

name: Ryan McJob
caption: "The Human Blob," a heavyset enhancement wrestler brought out by Tony Cage for an impromptu squash and submitted with a half Boston crab.

name: Mark McQueen
caption: A Society of Doom enforcer, billed as "The Tasmanian Devil," teaming with Marcus O'Malley to beat Sonicman and the Original Masked Man before entering the Gauntlet battle royal.

tenures.note: Teams with Marcus O'Malley for the Society of Doom against Blaze and The Real Deal on Firestorm (27 May 2004), then eliminates Orion in a mutual elimination in the Dog Day One tag team battle royal. Barred from competing in the Dog Day Two tag bracket's first round by majority owner Kingston Cash over an unspecified contractual problem. Returns to box with Orion during the sixteen-man tag scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004), credited alongside Marcus O'Malley as a winner when O'Malley unhooks the ring. Walks off during the Dog Days Four Tag Team Scramble on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004), abandoning partner Austin Lee, then is busted open by The Reckoning and eliminated from the tag Pentagon of Pain on Dog Day Five (16 July 2004). Won the ten-man tag for the Society of Doom on Wrestle Style V.1, challenged for the VWF Tag Team Championship alongside Marcus O'Malley on Wrestle Style V.2 (won by disqualification, titles retained), then lost to a returning wrestler billed "Orion #2" by count-out in the opening round of the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament on Wrestle Style V.3. Loses to Sebastian by rollup in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004). Wins with Marcus O'Malley over The Mighty Men by disqualification on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004) after being isolated and injured; is shown kidnapped on a video screen the prior week, forcing O'Malley from a Heavyweight title fatal four-way. Submits Real Deal with the Devils Snare to win the VWF Tag Team Championship with Marcus O'Malley from Blaze and Real Deal at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), billed Alcoholics Anonymous; the reinstated Rodeo Boys beat down both new champions immediately after. Survives the branding-iron chaos that costs Marcus O'Malley the use of his own arm, defending the VWF Tag Team Championship on March To Hell (21 October 2004) despite the Rodeo Boys' own interference. Successfully defends the titles again alongside a substitute Outlaw Morris Bass on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), submitting Billy Bones with the Devils Snare while an injured O'Malley cheers from his hospital bed. Gives a sullen, one-word prediction ("Pain") to Lean Darlene Orion and successfully defends his own half of the VWF Tag Team Championship over Robbie Caldwell in the Rage in the Cage at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), retaining alongside new co-champion Kevin Simmons after O'Malley is pinned. Defends his half of the VWF Tag Team Championship in a straight singles match against The Reckoning on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004) after The Salvation publicly refuses Kingston Cash's proposed handicap-match stipulation on The Mighty Men's own behalf, submitting The Reckoning with the Devils Snare. Retains automatically when mystery entrant Thunder Valenkov wins the battle royal for co-champion Kevin Simmons's own suspended half of the title on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004). Teams with Valenkov and 24 Hour Champion Adam Jennings to beat a short-handed Riders of the Apocalypse on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005), not wrestling himself as Jennings pins Robbie Caldwell. Teams with Thunder Valenkov in a non-title tag against Fast Eddie Cutlass and G-Gangsta on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), ruled a no contest after the Riders of the Apocalypse run in on former member G-Gangsta; runs down with Valenkov afterward to chase off Robbie Caldwell and Billy Bones from the VWF 24 Hour Championship match. Teams with Thunder Valenkov in a Rings Of Glory match against the Rodeo Boys at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), tapping out to Kenny Kidd's own Elko Lasso and eliminated from his own ring, but the VWF Tag Team Championship is retained regardless when Valenkov, already through Billy Bones, finishes Kidd alone with the Thunder Bomb. Challenges Sidious The Clown for the VWF Submission Championship at March To Madness (2 March 2005), caught in a Sleeper after an unexplained arena blackout and pinned. Loses the VWF Tag Team Championship with Thunder Valenkov at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) in an impromptu three-way after Team Brittania's own Simon Davidson pins Frank O'Shea instead of either champion. Challenges the champions Team Brittania for the titles at End Of March (30 March 2005) with Valenkov, winning by disqualification after the returning Hot Property run in on him. name: Kingston Cash
caption: The VWF's incoming 75% majority owner, introducing himself mid-broadcast and firing Fast Eddie Cutlass live during the closing battle royal.

tenures.note: Appears unnamed in two earlier backstage segments, as a shadowy figure dealing with Blackbird and Lark Fenriz, before his on-air introduction. Confirms Sebastian as Sonicman's new manager and enters Sonicman in the Dog Days tournament as a singles competitor. Scratches champion Lark Fenriz from his own match, bars Mark McQueen from the tag bracket over an unspecified contractual problem, then has Marcus O'Malley blindfolded and handcuffed for the tag final before ordering him into a handicap match against Sonicman and Sebastian; also announces Kevin Blair's VWF 24 Hour Championship defense against Flash as that week's elimination match, all on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004). Chokeslammed by The Outlaw Morris Bass on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) after warning him off violence, and removed from the arena on a stretcher; the night's tag and singles elimination matches are decided by random draw in his absence. Rebrands the broadcast Wrestle Style and strips Kevin Blair of recognition as 24 Hour Champion on Wrestle Style V.1; beats Kagedo in their Company vs. Suspension match on Wrestle Style V.2 after Kagedo's own knee gives out, suspending him six months without pay, then announces a random-draw VWF Heavyweight Title tournament; presides over the tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 and reveals a contract stipulation releasing both Rodeo Boys from the VWF after Billy Bones's title match loss. Rules that a double count-out and a title-match time-limit draw both leave every wrestler in the Heavyweight tournament on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004), then refuses to recognize Adam Jennings as new 24 Hour Champion despite his own battle royal win, unless Jennings takes the belt from Kevin Blair by force. Hires G-Gangsta as his own personal bodyguard against Jennings on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004). Announces a career-stakes ladder match between Iyasu Saku and Kevin Simmons for Vegas Violence on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), books Fast Eddie Cutlass's mini-rumble win as a Submission title shot, and hosts the Fenriz-Equalizer contract signing that Jason Storm crashes. Hosts Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004): sets up Kevin Simmons's own career-stakes ladder match with a rigged choice of envelopes, then has him beaten down by Sebastian, G-Gangsta and Robbie Caldwell before the Society of Doom makes the save; accepts lawyer RAR's offer to reinstate the Rodeo Boys, who immediately beat down the new VWF Tag Team Champions. Suspends Flash and books him against Lark Fenriz on March To Hell (21 October 2004), then overrules Classy Joey Boy's own 25% ownership stake by asserting his own 75% control. Turns Mark McQueen's title defense into a handicap match by adding Billy Bones on March To Hell II (28 October 2004), then announces a twelve-man, two-story Rage in the Cage with the final three spots decided by battle royal. Makes the Number One Contenders match a weapons match for the Rodeo Boys alone at Phear Phantastic 2004 (8 November 2004), then applauds Trinity's own closing celebration. Proposes a tag-title handicap-match stipulation for Mark McQueen against The Salvation on Holiday Havoc I (19 November 2004), refused on the spot. Agrees to recognize Gods Tears's own self-arranged VWF Hardcore Championship invitational and suspends Trinity from the VWF through the end of the year on Holiday Havoc II (3 December 2004), re-booking their own scheduled six-man tag as a triple threat between Lark Fenriz, Fast Eddie Cutlass and Classy Joey Boy. Sees his own authority publicly overridden by newly arrived VWF guardian John Tyler on New Years Kick Off (19 January 2005). Confronts Classy Joey Boy and John Tyler backstage over the Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005) main event booking, then dons a referee's shirt to work a stretch of the VWF Vegas Heavyweight Championship match. Opens Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005) with a warning to Yancy Kilpatrick's own ownership group, John Tyler and Classy Joey Boy, sets Classy Joey Boy and Kagedo to open the Pre Gauntlet Gauntlet, and signs an impostor using the ring name Scott Starring to a VWF contract. Opens Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005) boasting of the show's own record buy rate, dismisses Henry Fish's own demand for a Scott Starring title shot by sending out Kagedo, works a guest angle into the Wheel Of Chaos main event through his own newly revealed brother Terrance Cash, and vows afterward that Classy Joey Boy and The Maquilladora will never hold a VWF title again while he owns 75% of the company. Books a five-way elimination match for St Patricks Day Massacre at March To Madness (2 March 2005), then is confronted by John Tyler on air, who announces the IRS has seized the VWF over misappropriated talent funds diverted to an offshore account bearing Kingston Cash's own name; Cash is fired and escorted out of the Orleans, his own 75% ownership stake seized pending a future auction.

name: Scott Starring aka Henry Fish
caption: An Orleans Arena janitor who found a 12 Days Tournament Silver Medal discarded by Scott Starring and used it to talk Kingston Cash into a VWF contract as "Scott Starring," debuting under the stolen name at Road To Rhyolite II.

tenures.note: Introduced backstage by majority owner Kingston Cash as newly signed 12 Days Tournament Silver Medalist Scott Starring on Road To Rhyolite (27 January 2005), revealed on the spot as a different man wearing the discarded medal and named Henry Fish. Wrestles his in-ring debut billed Scott Starring aka Henry Fish on Road To Rhyolite II (7 February 2005), beating Vegas Vic with a top-rope Starfall Splash. Demands a title shot as "Scott Starring" at Ghost Town Blues (17 February 2005), answered instead with an impromptu match against Kagedo, who ducks a wild right hand and finishes him with a Dragon Suplex. Loses to Kagedo at March To Madness (2 March 2005), disqualified for a low blow after demanding a rematch with Werewolf Gregorson. Loses to The Maquilladora at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005) after she confronts him over the real Scott Starring's own record. Declares at End Of March (30 March 2005) that he will bring Van Wild to appear alongside him at The Gauntlet. Billed Scott Starring alongside a stand-in wrestling as the absent Van Wild, loses the VWF Tag Team Championship match to Team Brittania on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), pinned by Simon Davidson.

name: Vegas Vic

tenures.note: Loses his own debut to Scott Starring aka Henry Fish, beaten down with fists and kicks before a top-rope Starfall Splash.

tenures.note: Introduced ringside as an honored VWF-era guest, his own career ended by a 1986 rock-climbing accident that cost him a leg. Knocked from his chair when Robbie Caldwell takes his own prosthetic leg to use as a weapon on Adam Jennings in the VWF 24 Hour Championship match, then knocks Caldwell down with a right jab and reclaims the leg.

name: Terrance Cash

tenures.note: Poses as a ringside doctor sent to treat champion The Equalizer's own bleeding during the Wheel Of Chaos main event, instead injecting challengers Classy Joey Boy and The Maquilladora so The Equalizer can pin both for the win. Revealed by name only after the bell as Kingston Cash's own younger brother.

name: Frank O'Shea
caption: Paddy O'Shea's own younger brother, a ringside interference specialist who graduates to full tag-team competition alongside him.

tenures.note: Accompanies brother Paddy at ringside at March To Madness (2 March 2005), punching Adam Jennings to break up a near-fall and cause the VWF 24 Hour Championship match's own disqualification finish, then rolls dice for a coming tag-team title shot. Teams with Billy Bones against champions Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov for the VWF Tag Team Championship at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), the match becoming a three-way when the debuting Team Brittania insert themselves; Team Brittania wins by pinning O'Shea. Teams with Paddy against Capsman and Lance Voltar at End Of March (30 March 2005), keeping Capsman busy while Paddy pins Voltar with a top-rope fist drop. Teams with brother Paddy against Capsman and Lance Voltar on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), on the losing end when Voltar pins Paddy.

name: The Mad Bomber
caption: A masked, unpredictable newcomer recruited into the Riders of the Apocalypse, wrestling with live pyrotechnics and a fear of dogs.

tenures.note: Debuts at March To Madness (2 March 2005) as the fourth member of the Riders of the Apocalypse, beating Lark Fenriz with a Sit Out Powerbomb after detonating a small explosive near the entranceway, then helps stablemate Mr Electricity Robbie Caldwell beat Thunder Valenkov with a smoke bomb and a chair shot. Challenges Adam Jennings for the VWF 24 Hour Championship at St Patricks Day Massacre (17 March 2005), disqualified for refusing to let a bomb-sniffing dog search his pockets. Challenges Jennings for the title again at End Of March (30 March 2005), pinned while stuck in a bulky training suit meant to guard against the dog; blinds The Maquilladora with a flash of light earlier the same show to help Caldwell beat her. Loses his in-ring debut against newcomer Stan Klenski on The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), pinned after a Full Nelson Face First off the top rope; does not enter the wing's own closing Gauntlet battle royal despite Robbie Caldwell's own demand for the match.
